articles.title: 600 marijuana plants, 1,400 seedlings seized in Ilocos Sur
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The police discovered and seized about 600 fully grown marijuana plants and 1,400 seedlings from three cultivation sites in Sugpon, Ilocos Sur, on Saturday. According to…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The police discovered and seized about 600 fully grown marijuana plants and 1,400 seedlings from three cultivation sites in Sugpon, Ilocos Sur, on Saturday.
According to the Ilocos Sur Police Provincial Office (ISPPO), the marijuana eradication operation was conducted in Barangay Caoayan, Sugpon, covering an estimated 111 square meters.

The operation was led by Lt. Col. David Dulnuan, deputy provincial director for operations, with personnel from the ISPPO Drug Enforcement Unit, 2nd Ilocos Sur Provincial Mobile Force Company, ISPPO Intelligence and Detective Management Unit-KIMAT, Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Region I and Sugpon police.
Police said the confiscated marijuana plants and seedlings are worth an estimated P176,000.
The operation was part of the ISPPO’s continuing campaign to eliminate marijuana cultivation and curb the illegal drug trade in the province. (Kenneth P. Tabin/contibutor)

articles.title: Butuan City water crisis sparks calls for accountability, solutions
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Criticism of the Butuan City Water District (BCWD) and the city government has intensified as residents endure another round of water supply interruption, prompting…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Criticism of the Butuan City Water District (BCWD) and the city government has intensified as residents endure another round of water supply interruption, prompting calls for greater accountability and a long-term plan to secure the city’s water supply.
Posts on social media stated the recurring shortages could no longer be treated solely as an emergency caused by dry weather.
Consumers urged the BCWD and local officials to disclose what measures had been completed and how they intended to prevent similar crises.
The criticism followed the return of BCWD’s “Oplan Sag-Ob,” an emergency measure that allows concessionaires to fetch water from designated distribution stations when regular service is inadequate.
While residents acknowledged the importance of water rationing during emergencies, they said the program should not become a substitute for reliable infrastructure and long-term preparation.
“Emergency measures should remain emergency measures. They cannot become institutionalized substitutes for infrastructure,” Luna Kaisog stated.
Kaisog called on the BCWD to publicly present a comprehensive water security and drought resilience plan containing measurable targets, project costs and completion timelines.

The proposed plan should include projections of Butuan’s water demand, the condition of existing pumping stations, reservoirs and wells, possible alternative sources, additional storage requirements, watershed protection measures and targets for reducing water lost through leaks and other causes, she said.
Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” Fortun raised the water shortage issue during his State of the City Address on Aug. 5.

Fortun said water supply remained the responsibility of the BCWD, but disclosed that the city government had purchased three submersible pumps to help improve water pressure, particularly during dry periods.
He, however, acknowledged that these interventions would not be enough to solve the city’s water problems.

On Aug. 24, BCWD reported that the Taguibo watershed had experienced 23 days without sufficient rainfall. Streamflow had declined to about 42 million to 43 million liters a day, while the dam level had dropped to 3.58 meters—below the four-meter critical threshold.
The deterioration prompted the water district to resume “Oplan Sag-Ob (Fetch Water)”
Resident Allen Kenneth Pacis questioned why stronger contingency measures had not been put in place despite earlier indications of a potentially severe dry period.
Pacis said the water shortage affected not only households and businesses but also hospitals and patients, including those undergoing dialysis who depend on a reliable water supply for treatment.
“This is not simply an inconvenience,” he said, warning that disruptions in essential services could have serious consequences for patients.

Netizens called on the city government and the water district to publish project timelines, expected additional capacity and contingency measures that could be activated before water levels reach critical thresholds.
The BCWD and the city government have not issued a detailed response to the criticisms and proposals. /gsg

articles.title: Nigeria: Suspected oil thieves killed after inhaling fumes
articles.summary: PORT HARCOURT, Nigeria — At least 37 people died early Thursday in Nigeria’s oil-rich southern Niger Delta after inhaling fumes during the theft of fuel from a pipeline, a local NGO said.…

blocks.text: PORT HARCOURT, Nigeria — At least 37 people died early Thursday in Nigeria’s oil-rich southern Niger Delta after inhaling fumes during the theft of fuel from a pipeline, a local NGO said.
Illegal oil-siphoning is a major problem in Nigeria — an OPEC member and one of Africa’s largest petroleum producers — causing serious pollution.
Accidents are common in swamps in the Niger Delta, where smugglers tap into pipelines to steal crude and refine it into fuel for sale.

The Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre (YEAC-Nigeria) said it had “received and confirmed a report from its network of youth volunteers and human rights defenders in the Niger Delta in the Okrika Local Government Area of Rivers State that some persons, not fewer than 37 have been confirmed dead after inhaling ‘Indorama fuel’.”
It said in a statement that those killed are “suspected to be oil thieves”, adding: “Many others are still missing.”

It said “youths had connected a pipe to a tapping point on a pipeline that normally transports” crude from producer Indorama Eleme Petrochemical through the Port Harcourt Refinery to vessels loading for export.
The men tapped into the pipeline and were loading oil into their own boats, it said.
“Many are still missing, and some corpses have been seen floating on the river but have not yet been recovered,” the organisation said.
Oil pollution
Rivers State police confirmed the incident in a statement saying the victims were allegedly attempting to steal oil, but it did not give a toll.
The Niger Delta is home to Nigeria’s multi-billion-dollar oil and gas resources, but residents of the region live in poverty due to decades of oil exploration, neglect and pollution.
The opposition party African Democratic Congress blamed the accident on the “economic situation in the country” which it said forces people to take desperate action.
The party’s candidate Atiku Abubakar will challenge President Bola Tinubu in elections in January.
When he came into office in 2023, Tinubu introduced tough economic reforms that triggered high inflation, soaring fuel prices and rising poverty.
YEAC-Nigeria called “on the government to provide alternative livelihood opportunities”, including “the legalization of artisanal refining”. /dl

articles.title: Influencer boom at US Open tests boundaries of tennis etiquette
articles.summary: The growing love affair between influencers and the premier American tennis event has caused some growing pains

blocks.text: SPORTS FASHION. Japan's Naomi Osaka enters the court before her second round match against Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova at the US Open.
Robert Deutsch/IMAGN IMAGES/Reuters
The growing love affair between influencers and the premier American tennis event has caused some growing pains

items: The US Open has seen a significant presence of influencers and content creators, with around 100 granted credentials, including 20 focused on food and beverage coverage.
The trend has led to disruptions during matches, prompting criticism from players like Naomi Osaka and Jessica Pegula, who expressed concerns over respect for the sport and its etiquette.

Despite the challenges, some players acknowledge the potential benefits of influencers in promoting tennis to wider audiences, though they emphasize the need for better management of their presence at the event.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NEW YORK, USA – Influencers and content creators armed with smartphones and ring lights have featured prominently in the stands at this year’s US Open, as they try to grab the spotlight away from the on-court action at one of tennis’ marquee events.

Around 100 content creators were given credentials for the tournament, organizers said, with 20 of those dedicated to providing coverage of the food and beverage scene alone, where caviar-topped chicken nuggets and the famed “Honey Deuce” cocktail promise viral attention.
@elirallo #usopen #honeyd ♬ original sound – Eli Rallo
Thousands more amateur social media hounds can be found throughout the plaza and in the stands — after shelling out for their own tickets.
“I feel like every Slam kind of has their own identity and the US Open has kind of always been the ‘big-show Grand Slam,'” said the 2017 finalist Madison Keys.

Celebrities have long been ubiquitous in the stands — from A-list stars to US President Donald Trump — as the ultra-wealthy shell out thousands of dollars for seats at the see-and-be-seen event of New York’s summer sporting calendar.
But the growing love affair between influencers and the premier American tennis event has caused some growing pains.

A chair umpire was forced to reprimand a group of patrons for staging a disruptive photo shoot while two-time US Open champion Naomi Osaka was serving during her first-round win against Anastasia Zakharova on Monday.

This was one of the cringiest things I’ve ever seen live. The US Open used to be an actual tennis tournament https://t.co/1kAYND6VOe pic.twitter.com/c1jbi4lUlQ— Danny Singer (@michiganboy310) September 2, 2026
“Obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport,” Osaka told reporters on Thursday after her second-round win over Katerina Siniakova.

“It could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like first-round match.”

Another social media user attracted attention for all the wrong reasons when she posted a series of photos posing inside Arthur Ashe Stadium while Keys was in the middle of playing a point against Alina Korneeva, which breached basic tennis etiquette.
“I can appreciate the influencers coming and kind of showcasing the US Open experience,” said 2024 runner-up Jessica Pegula.

“But I do think that it’s tough when you see videos like that when they’re taking pictures and using the selfie lights. People are down there trying to perform, and it’s their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful.
“I think it’s gotten a little maybe too much.”

The trend is a direct result of the tournament’s popularity, with surging attendance leading organizers to expand the main draw action to 15 days. The tournament was further expanded with the mixed doubles competition being held as a standalone event the week before singles action kicks off.
The men’s ATP tour expanded its partnership with TikTok earlier this year, citing a more than 25% increase in posts under #tennis during 2025.
“The more we try to raise awareness about tennis, the better it is, the more popular the sport is,” said 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev.

“For sure, if it disturbs during the play, like if you see the light or something, well, you always say to the referee, can be sometimes challenging, like if during the point this happens.” – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Although the eastern state accounts for less than 3% of the nationwide electorate, the election outcome could serve as a bellwether about the far-right AFD's prospects in the rest of the country. DW…

image.caption: The far-right AfD is polling strongly in Saxony-Anhalt, while the BSW is seeking a first foothold in the state parliamentImage: Michael Taeger/Jan Huebner/IMAGO

blocks.text: Live

Although the eastern state accounts for less than 3% of the nationwide electorate, the election outcome could serve as a bellwether about the far-right AFD's prospects in the rest of the country. DW has the latest.

blocks.caption: The far-right AfD is polling strongly in Saxony-Anhalt, while the BSW is seeking a first foothold in the state parliamentImage: Michael Taeger/Jan Huebner/IMAGO

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: Saxony-Anhalt voters are set to elect a new state parliament in a vote being closely watched across Germany
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is polling well ahead of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which has led the state government since 2002
The result could test Germany's political 'firewall' against the far right and put pressure on CDU Chancellor Friedrich Merz if the CDU performs badly

blocks.text: It is election day in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt state. Follow all the developments here.
September 6, 2026
ANALYSIS: Why is this election so closely watched?
I have not experienced a more polarizing election since Brexit or Trump vs. Hillary Clinton in 2016. That is because the stakes are so high.
For a number of reasons, the decision voters in Saxony-Anhalt reach today is being watched closely in Berlin and beyond:

items: Watershed moment: Should the AfD secure an absolute majority, it would be the first time a right-wing populist party has won power in a state in Germany in the postwar era.

Firewall: Should the AfD not secure an absolute majority, the focus will turn to the conservative CDU. Pressure will mount on the party to rethink its longstanding policy of not governing with or passing laws with the far-right AfD or far-left Left Party. Such a debate risks splitting the CDU.

Chancellor: A dire result for the conservatives may lead to calls for the deeply unpopular Chancellor Friedrich Merz to be replaced. In CDU circles in Berlin, the talk is of an election that could 'change the republic.'

articles.title: Egypt sentences TV presenter, 11 others to death in drugs case
articles.summary: CAIRO — An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drugs case, official media reported on…

blocks.text: CAIRO — An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drugs case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her program “Mission Impossible”, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

The state-linked Al-Ahram newspaper said a Cairo court sentenced “Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging on charges of forming an organized criminal gang specializing in procuring materials used in manufacturing narcotics, with the intent to traffic them, and possessing and carrying unlicensed firearms and ammunition”.
The verdict came after the court consulted the Grand Mufti of Egypt for his religious opinion, a procedure required by Egyptian law in capital cases.
The verdict is subject to appeal.
Khalifa also owns a plastic surgery clinic and a production company that specializes in organizing parties and events.

According to the state-run Akhbar Al-Youm newspaper, the defendants were charged with “manufacturing synthetic drugs with the intent to traffic them, by importing the materials used in manufacturing from abroad”.
Al-Ahram reported that authorities seized more than 750 kilograms of narcotics and raw materials, and found two apartments used as laboratories as well as unlicensed firearms and ammunition.
The court also sentenced Khalifa and others to five years in prison over a separate case involving the kidnapping and assault of a young man.
Egypt applies the death penalty for premeditated murder, terrorism, some rape offences and drug trafficking.
According to the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms, 541 death sentences were issued in Egypt in 2025. /dl

articles.title: Logs, debris clog waterways in flood-hit Bataan village
articles.summary: DINALUPIHAN, Bataan — Logs, tree branches and firewood clogged waterways and the Pita River in Barangay Pita, an area severely affected by flooding in this landlocked town. The river overflowed and…

blocks.text: DINALUPIHAN, Bataan — Logs, tree branches and firewood clogged waterways and the Pita River in Barangay Pita, an area severely affected by flooding in this landlocked town.
The river overflowed and swept away at least nine houses near its banks on Sept. 2.
The Dinalupihan Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, together with local police, conducted forced evacuations of residents in affected areas.

Residents who posted their concerns on social media said the logs and other debris may have come from neighboring Zambales, noting that there had been no reported illegal logging activities in Dinalupihan.
They said the floodwaters, carrying logs and firewood, may have contributed to the river’s overflow and the destruction of houses.

articles.title: Israel army says striking southern Lebanon, urges evacuation
articles.summary: JERUSALEM — The Israeli military said on Sunday it was carrying out strikes in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched drones at its soldiers, and urged residents of the town of Arab Salim to…

blocks.text: JERUSALEM — The Israeli military said on Sunday it was carrying out strikes in southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched drones at its soldiers, and urged residents of the town of Arab Salim to evacuate.

“Terrorists from the Hezbollah terrorist organization launched two drones towards IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon,” the military said in a statement, adding that there were no reports of Israeli soldiers wounded.
“This constitutes a blatant violation by the Hezbollah terrorist organization. In response, the IDF is now striking in southern Lebanon.”
In another message, the Israeli military warned residents of Arab Salim to leave ahead of imminent attacks.
“You are situated near a facility belonging to the terrorist organisation Hezbollah, against which the IDF will be operating,” it wrote in Arabic on Telegram.

Lebanon was drawn into the Middle East war in March after Iran-backed Hezbollah attacked Israel, which responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
Violence has lessened since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding on the broader conflict in June and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon later that month.
Israeli forces are operating inside a self-declared “security zone” around 10 kilometers (six miles) deep inside Lebanon along the border.
Authorities in Lebanon said on Saturday that Israeli strikes killed four people in the country’s south and east. /dl

articles.title: Sara Duterte accuses DILG of political harassment over 'surveillance'
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday accused the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) of political harassment, after DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said authorities knew her…

blocks.text: Published September 6, 2026 12:16pm

Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday accused the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) of political harassment after DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said authorities knew her whereabouts on the night an arrest warrant was issued against her.

Duterte made the accusation in response to Remulla’s earlier remarks addressing her distrust of the court and the police, saying, “We knew of her whereabouts the night before, but we did not force the warrant of arrest.”

According to Duterte, Remulla’s statement supposedly amounted to an admission by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other government agencies of a long-standing pattern of political harassment and surveillance against her.

“Ang mga salitang ito ni Secretary Jonvic Remulla ay tila nagpapatibay sa mga dokumentong matagal na naming hawak hinggil sa harassment at surveillance operations ng Philippine National Police at iba pang ahensya ng gobyerno laban sa akin,” Duterte said in a statement.

(These words from Secretary Jonvic Remulla seem to confirm the documents we have long held regarding the harassment and surveillance operations of the Philippine National Police and other government agencies against me.)

Duterte alleged that the administration’s surveillance operations against her had been ongoing for several years, citing what she described as the government’s massive spending on activities targeting the incumbent vice president.
She also questioned why authorities had to visit her mother and children if they already knew her whereabouts.
“At dahil alam ninyo kung nasaan ako, isang mahalagang tanong ang dapat ninyong sagutin—bakit ninyo pa kinakailangang puntahan ang aking ina at mga anak?” the vice president said.
(And because you knew where I was, there is an important question you need to answer—why did you still need to go to my mother and my children?)
“Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya,” she added.
(There is only one clear answer—to intimidate and frighten my family.)
Duterte also reiterated that she could not surrender to the police because she said authorities could not guarantee her safety while in custody.

“Nais ko mang bigyang-diin ang aming posisyon ukol sa isyu ng jurisdiction sa pamamagitan ng pagsuko sa pulisya, hindi ko magawa dahil hindi ninyo kayang ipangako na magiging ligtas ako sa loob ng inyong kulungan. Hindi ninyo maipangako na hindi ako sasaktan o aabusuhin habang nasa inyong kustodiya,” Duterte said.

(I want to emphasize our position on the issue of jurisdiction by surrendering to the police, but I cannot do so because you cannot promise that I will be safe inside your jail. You cannot promise that I will not be hurt or abused while in your custody.)
“...Wala kaming tiwala sa iyo, Jonvic Remulla, at sa mga pulis na sunod-sunuran sa isang korap na pamahalaang pinamumunuan ni Marcos,” she added.
(...We have no trust in you, Jonvic Remulla, and in the police officers who blindly follow a corrupt government led by Marcos.)
Duterte also cited her camp’s previous allegations concerning the circumstances surrounding former President Rodrigo Duterte’s arrest and transfer to The Hague.
In a message sent via Viber on Sunday, Remulla said it is not "illegal" or "unusual" for the DILG to know Duterte's location since it is part of the department's duty.

"She should blame the people around her. They informed us where she was when the warrant was issued. It’s our duty to do our best to know her location. That was not illegal nor unusual," Remulla told GMA News Online.
The Vice President was issued an arrest warrant on Friday after a Quezon City court found probable cause to charge her with three counts of grave threats.

The charges stem from Duterte’s public statements in 2024 that she had hired an assassin to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez if an alleged plot to kill her succeeded.
On Saturday, she posted bail of at least P360,000 before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court. —with a report from Mariel Celine Serquiña/MCG/RF, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Nobody will win’: Zelenskyy adviser warns of mutual destruction if war with Russia continues
articles.summary:
Serhii Beskrestnov says deadlock on frontline and increasing use of deep strikes is placing civilians and infrastructure at greater risk

Russia and Ukraine are locked in an escalating war of…

blocks.text: Russia and Ukraine are locked in an escalating war of long-range strikes with a growing risk to civilians in which neither side can entirely prevail, according to Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s defence technology adviser.

Serhii Beskrestnov, widely known by his call sign, Flash, said he was worried about the prospects for Kyiv this winter, and suggested elderly people should be evacuated in case Russian bombing were to knock out the capital’s energy supply.

However, the rapid wartime evolution also gave Ukraine the means to strike back, with plans to launch 1,000 drones a night to strike economic and military targets in Russia and halt its commercial air traffic, he said.

“Now, this is a war of cities, a war of infrastructure,” Beskrestnov told the Guardian, describing a conflict that is essentially deadlocked on the frontline, with civilians at increasing risk hundreds of miles away.

“In this war, nobody will win this game, because both countries, after the war, will have destroyed economics, infrastructures. So it’s stupid. We should stop this war. We proposed to Russia to stop this war, but Russia does not want to stop,” he said.

blocks.caption: The ruins of the Rozetka e-commerce distribution hub in Brovary, Kyiv, after Russian strikes in early August. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Beskrestnov, 51, a radio specialist, was first appointed by the former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov as a technology adviser in January, before being taken on directly in July, after the latter’s dismissal.

The adviser, who survived a drone attack on his home in April, agreed that “attack had become more powerful than defence”, because both sides’ air defences could not keep up with the number of missiles and drones available.

Russia could engage in a sustained bombing of electricity, water and heating systems in Kyiv this winter with the high-speed ballistic missiles it was producing at a rate of more than 100 a month, Beskrestnov said.
Earlier this week, Vladimir Putin said Russia’s military had been “ordered to prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities, showing no sign of halting the war.

“For me, it’s horrible,” Beskrestnov said. “We are talking about 2 to 3 million people, and Russia understands it can create a disaster in Kyiv.” City authorities should think about evacuating civilians in advance, particularly elderly people, he added, while emphasising he was not making an official statement.

blocks.caption: People gathered outside after a Russian attack in the Solomianskyi district of Kyiv last month. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Ukraine is desperately short of US Patriot air defence interceptors, the main weapon capable of halting ballistic missiles, and Beskrestnov said he was “not sure” that Zelenskyy could obtain enough from abroad to prevent a crisis. Last month, the president said he wanted to secure 300 Patriot interceptors for the winter.

Beskrestnov predicted Ukraine would “attack Russia more and more with deep strikes”, continuing a campaign that has resulted in factories, warehouses and oil refineries being bombed. “We have a target from our president to increase the quantity of attacks to 1,000 a day,” he said, rising from its current level of about 300.

blocks.caption: Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced this week that Ukraine would attempt to use drones to halt civilian aviation in Russia. Photograph: David Levene/The Guardian

blocks.text: Addressing Zelenskyy’s announcement this week that there would be a sustained attempt by Ukraine to halt civil aviation inside Russia with the drones, Beskrestnov said: “I think it’s very simple: it’s not necessary for us to attack an airport, it’s just enough for us to fly at the airport and the airport will be closed.”

Russia has also made a series of advances that have boosted its attack potential, including its first suspected use of artificial intelligence. Ukrainian investigators concluded that a simple Molniya drone that killed a person near a Zaporizhzhia gas station in July was being guided not by radio but by AI.
after newsletter promotion

“I’m just afraid what happens in the future because I think it’s just a question of time before Russia installs this technology in a Shahed,” he said, referring to the country’s standard long-range drone. It could render Ukraine’s “huge jamming network” obsolete without any radio communication to jam.
Beskrestnov said Ukraine was working on its own autonomous drones – “We have a prototype” – but that he believed Russia appeared to have more scale right now.

Russia has also developed a new wave of drones and missiles powered by Chinese-made jet engines that can fly at more than 200mph (320km/h), faster than the first generation of cheap Shahed interceptors that Ukraine has developed.

Moscow fired 2,500 jet-powered Shahed drones into Ukraine in August, up from 1,500 in July, and was planning to make “about 36,000 in 2027”, Beskrestnov said. It also planned to build another 30,000 of the slower piston-engine type next year.

Jet-powered Shaheds are already being used to threaten Kyiv and other big cities for hours at a time, but they will be complemented by another 10,000 cheap Banderol cruise missiles during 2027, plus a further 10,000 Dan-T missiles, boosting Russia’s ability to bomb Ukraine’s infrastructure.

blocks.caption: People sleeping at Dorohozhychi subway station because of the threat of Russian night attacks. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: Four to six Ukrainian companies were working on jet interceptors, Beskrestnov said, but they were “not ready for final production”, giving Moscow a window of advantage. The adviser would not give a timeframe for when the interceptors would be ready. At present, fighter jets take the lead in shooting down jet drones.

Civilian casualties have been rising as long-range attacks increase. According to the UN, 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July (the last month for which figures are available), the highest since March 2022. Accurate figures for Russia are not readily available.

Beskrestnov said the dismissal of Fedorov as defence minister after a clash with Zelenskyy was “a pity”, though the change in his own role meant the scope of his work had expanded beyond the armed forces to include the national guard and across government.
His role, he said, was technical and advisory and he sought to avoid becoming embroiled in personality clashes. “Don’t mix me with politics. Politics always has a part of garbage, rubbish,” he said.

articles.title: Inflation among poor households surges in Western Visayas
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — Inflation among the bottom 30 percent of households in Western Visayas rose to 9.8 percent in July, with the rate reaching 12.5 percent in Iloilo province, government data showed. The…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — Inflation among the bottom 30 percent of households in Western Visayas rose to 9.8 percent in July, with the rate reaching 12.5 percent in Iloilo province, government data showed.
The regional rate was higher than the 8.2 percent recorded nationwide for the same income group in July, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).

In Iloilo province, inflation among poor households rose from 9.3 percent in June to 12.5 percent in July. Aklan followed at 11.3 percent, up from 9.6 percent in June, while Antique recorded 10.2 percent.
Inflation among poor households in Iloilo City stood at 9.3 percent, compared with 5.7 percent in Guimaras and 3.9 percent in Capiz.
Western Visayas’ July rate was a sharp increase from negative 1.1 percent recorded in the same month last year.

Nationally, inflation among the bottom 30 percent remained at 8.2 percent in August, up sharply from negative 0.6 percent in August 2025. The average rate for the group stood at 6.2 percent from January to August.
Food and non-alcoholic beverages remained the biggest source of price pressure, accounting for 52.5 percent of overall inflation among poor households in August.
Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels contributed 18.9 percent, while transportation accounted for 12 percent.

Rice remained a major driver. Rice inflation among the bottom 30 percent accelerated to 22.5 percent in August from 19.3 percent in July, even as overall food inflation eased to 8.3 percent from 8.5 percent.
The PSA said it measures inflation for the bottom 30 percent separately because poorer households devote a larger share of their income to food and other basic necessities.
The agency has yet to release detailed August provincial figures for the bottom 30 percent in Western Visayas.

Outside Metro Manila, inflation among poor households accelerated to 8.4 percent in August from 8.3 percent in July, while the rate in the National Capital Region eased to 4.3 percent from 4.5 percent.
This meant poor households outside Metro Manila faced inflation nearly twice the rate recorded in the capital region. /gsg

articles.title: LTFRB opens 8,750 slots for TNVS units in Metro Manila, Ilocos, Bicol
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has opened a total of 8,750 slots for transport network vehicle service (TNVS) units in Metro Manila and the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has opened a total of 8,750 slots for transport network vehicle service (TNVS) units in Metro Manila and the Ilocos and Bicol regions to address the increasing demand for public transportation.

The LTFRB announced on Sunday that 7,500 TNVS slots allotted in Metro Manila will be exclusive for electric vehicles that include Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) and Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs).
LTFRB Acting Chairperson Greg Pua said this was in line with the government’s directive for a “modern and environment-friendly public transportation.”

“Conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) other than PHEVs, and other vehicle technologies that do not fall within the BEV or PHEV classifications shall not be eligible for the slots opened herein,” the LTFRB Memorandum Circular 2026-084 stated.

“The classification of the vehicle as a BEV or PHEV shall be based on its registration and classification by the Land Transportation Office (LTO) and other applicable government standards and issuances,” it added.
The LTFRB also allotted 650 slots for Ilocos Region for electric vehicles, of which 75 slots each were for internal combustion engines and non-internal combustion engines in Ilocos Norte.
It noted that the same allocation was given to Ilocos Sur and La Union.
A total of 200 slots were allotted for Pangasinan, of which 100 slots each were given to internal combustion engines and non-internal combustion engines.
The agency also shared that 600 slots were approved for Bicol Region, of which half were for electric vehicles.

Pua said that the opening of slots was based on the monitoring and study that revealed the insufficient TNVS allocation amid the increasing number of commuters in Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, and Bicol Region.
He also said that the agency also considered feedback from various stakeholders.

“A separate review and study pointed to increased economic activities as one of the major factors—expanding urban, commercial, government, and tourism centers that generate increasing demand for safe, reliable, accessible, and technology-enabled transport services for residents and visitors,” the LTFRB said.
The LTFRB said it will start processing the application for the available slots once the memorandum circular has been published in a newspaper of general circulation. /gsg

articles.title: Indonesia: Flights canceled as Anak Krakatau volcano erupts
articles.summary: The spread of ash after the volcanic eruption of Anak Krakatau has impacted thousands of passengers, as flights were canceled at Jakarta's international airport.

image.caption: The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau saw lava sprouting and spewing of ash that was detected even 150 kilometers awayImage: PVMBG/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Hundreds of flights were canceled at Jakarta's international airport after Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano erupted early Sunday morning, more than 150 kilometers (93 miles) away.
The volcano produced a fountain of lava and loud sounds heard up to 700 kilometres (435 miles) away, Indonesia's geological agency said in a statement.

The cloud of ash was detected up to a height of 6,000 meters (20,000 feet) on the Java side of the volcano and a plume of up to 15,000 meters (50,000 feet) on the ‌Sumatra side and some parts of Banten province in Java, the ‌meteorological ​agency BMKG posted on its website.
No incidents of casualties were reported, and no evacuation orders were issued.
Danger remains in Indonesia in the wake of volcano eruptions
The closest township is more than 16 kilometers (10 miles) away, but the authorities warned residents and visitors to stay at least 3 kilometers (1.9 miles) from the volcano's active crater.
Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned.
Indonesia cancels flights
The ash spread across parts of the capital Jakarta and Lampung province on the southern tip of Sumatra island, Indonesia's Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said.
The spread of ash after the volcanic eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta's international airport.
Soekarno-Hatta International Airport posted on ‌Instagram that it had ⁠suspended ⁠flight operations until 9:30 a.m. (0230 GMT) due to volcanic ash.
New volcano eruptions hit Indonesia
"Due to increased activity from the Mount Anak Krakatau eruption, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has temporarily suspended flight operations from 5:30 a.m. to 9.30 a.m.," the airport said.
The disruption of flight operations has impacted more than 22,000 passengers, the transport ministry said in a statement, adding that 209 flights were affected, particularly to and from Singapore.
Anak Krakatau lies in the middle between Java and Sumatra in Indonesia's vast island chain, which sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire," where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are frequent.
Anak Krakatau means "Child of Krakatau." The volcano is the offspring of the famous Krakatau, whose monumental eruption in 1883 triggered a period of global cooling.

Robert Deutsch/IMAGN IMAGES/Reuters
Alex Eala squanders a 4-2 lead in the deciding set as she falls short of a fourth-round berth at the US Open and remains winless against Iva Jovic

items: Alex Eala lost to American world No. 14 Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open, marking her third defeat against Jovic in their WTA Tour meetings.
Eala had a strong performance, leading 4-2 in the deciding set, but ultimately lost the match 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 after a 3-hour marathon.
Despite the loss, Eala's run at the US Open was commendable, surpassing her previous year's performance and showcasing her growth as a player.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The third time, unfortunately, did not prove to be the charm for Alex Eala.

Eala remained winless against American world No. 14 Iva Jovic as she exited the US Open with a stinging 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 loss in the third round at the famed Arthur Ashe Stadium in Flushing Meadows, New York, on Saturday, September 5 (Sunday, September 6, Manila time).

Up 4-2 in the deciding set, the Filipina world No. 18 ran out of steam when it mattered most, sending her finest run in the final Grand Slam of the tennis calendar to a heartbreaking end at the hands of her close friend.

Eala fell to 0-3 against Jovic in their WTA Tour meetings after losing in straight sets in the opening round of the French Open in May and again in the second round of the Queen’s Club Championships in June.
But Eala, at one point, seemed poised for a breakthrough win over Jovic.
Playing in primetime at the world’s largest tennis stadium with a roaring crowd behind her, Eala finally took a set from Jovic and even grabbed a 4-2 lead in the decider.
Jovic, however, dug deep and won four of the last five games to come out triumphant in the 3-hour, 3-minute marathon and arrange a fourth-round clash with compatriot Coco Gauff.
Eala showed some resistance during that stretch as she saved a match point in the 10th game to knot the score at 5-5 before Jovic clinched the next two games.

Seeded 14th, Jovic moved to a second match point with a booming forehand winner, then sealed the victory when Eala dumped a shot into the net — the American falling flat on her back in tears after advancing to the US Open round of 16 for the first time in her career.
“I don’t even know what to say, that felt like a marathon and I felt like I lost my sanity five times over to win that match,” said Jovic.
“But it’s really worth it for this feeling. I’m usually not one to show that many emotions but this one really meant a lot to me so it’s everything to have another match here at the US Open.”

It was a painful exit for Eala as she came oh-so close to matching her best Grand Slam campaign, a fourth-round appearance in the Wimbledon Championships in July where she dethroned Poland’s Iga Swiatek in the third round.
Eala flashed a smile as she thanked the fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium, but the disappointment of the loss finally sank in as she fought back tears on her way to the dugout.

Still, it was a commendable run for Eala as she surpassed her showing last year, when she fell to Spain’s Cristina Bucsa in the second round after making history as the first Filipino to win a Grand Slam main draw match in the Open era following an upset of Denmark’s Clara Tauson.
This year, Eala swatted aside USA’s Mary Stoiana, 6-1, 6-2, to open her campaign, and then made quick work of Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova, 6-1, 6-4. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Calabarzon measles-rubella vaccination hits 56.8% of target population
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The measles-rubella vaccination campaign in the Calabarzon region reached 56.8 percent of its target population in 20 days , according to the Department of Health Center for Health…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The measles-rubella vaccination campaign in the Calabarzon region reached 56.8 percent of its target population in 20 days , according to the Department of Health Center for Health Development (DOH-CHD) Calabarzon.
Based on the agency’s accomplishment tracker, 758,454 children had received measles-rubella (MR) vaccines as of 10 p.m. Friday.
The DOH-CHD had targeted 1,335,685 children 6 to 59 months old across Calabarzon under the Ligtas Tigdas 2026: Measles-Rubella Supplemental Immunization Activity (MR SIA).
Meanwhile, 674,754 children had received vitamin A supplementation, equivalent to 47 percent of the region’s target population of 1,436,443.
The MR SIA was originally scheduled from Aug. 10 to 28 but was extended until Sept. 4 due to heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” in recent weeks.
Despite falling short of its target, the DOH-CHD described the campaign as a success, citing the collective efforts of health workers, partners and communities.

“Ligtas Tigdas is a success shared by everyone. Every vaccine administered, every piece of information shared, and every child protected is the result of our collective action and concern for their well-being,” the agency said.
The DOH-CHD also thanked its partners, particularly the Philippine Red Cross, for helping implement the vaccination campaign.
“As this campaign comes to an end, let us continue working together to protect the health of every child in Calabarzon,” the agency said.
Among the provinces and cities in the region, Laguna recorded the highest vaccination coverage, with 192,027 children, or 71.7 percent of its target population of 267,908, vaccinated.

It was followed by Cavite (199,834 of its 368,263 target children vaccinated, or 54.3 percent), Batangas (139,300 of 258,969, or 53.8 percent), Quezon (98,977 of 188,245, or 52.6 percent), Lucena City (14,290 of 27,987, or 51.1 percent) and Rizal (114,026 of 224,313, or 50.8 percent).

Despite health authorities’ assurance that measles-rubella vaccines are proven safe and effective and provide the best protection against the diseases and their potentially serious complications, misinformation and misconceptions circulating on social media have posed challenges to the immunization campaign.
Measles and rubella are caused by different viruses. Measles is caused by the rubeola virus, while rubella is caused by the rubella virus.
Both are highly contagious diseases but can be prevented through vaccination.

DOH data showed that the Philippines recorded 1,627 measles and rubella cases from Jan. 4 to March 21 this year, a 45 percent increase from the 1,121 cases reported during the same period in 2025. /gsg

articles.title: Indonesia’s main airport suspends operations after volcanic eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA — Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday due to ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano, more than 150 kilometers away. Mount Anak…

blocks.text: JAKARTA — Indonesia halted operations at its main international airport outside Jakarta on Sunday due to ash spewed from the Anak Krakatoa volcano, more than 150 kilometers away.
Mount Anak Krakatoa erupted on Saturday, producing a fountain of lava and booming sounds that could be heard up to 700 kilometres (435 miles) away, the geology agency said in a statement.
Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned.
Ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, prompting authorities to suspend operations from 01:30 am Sunday (Saturday 1830 GMT).

“The latest paper test…showed positive results indicating the spread of volcanic ash in the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport area, consequently the airport closure was extended until Sunday at 09:30 am (0230 GMT),” the transport ministry said in a statement Sunday.
More than 22,000 passengers have been impacted by the suspension, the ministry said, adding that 209 flights were affected, in particular to and from Singapore.
Other affected international routes included Doha, Sydney, and Kuala Lumpur.
Anak Krakatoa, which means Child of Krakatoa, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
It has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa.
That disaster was one of the deadliest and most destructive in history with an estimated 35,000 people killed.
Indonesia, a Southeast Asian archipelago nation, sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where the meeting of continental plates causes high volcanic and seismic activity. /dl

articles.title: Barely saved, he cuts mourning short to help flood survivors
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Two seconds is time enough to blink. For 31-year-old Sudip Kumar Neupane, this window meant the difference between life and death. Sudip was racing back on a motorcycle after…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Two seconds is time enough to blink. For 31-year-old Sudip Kumar Neupane, this window meant the difference between life and death.
Sudip was racing back on a motorcycle after warning villagers of an approaching flood when buffaloes slowed him down by an estimated two seconds.
Then a torrent of flood and debris came.

As mud and rock and water barrelled down, carrying away his 27-year-old younger brother, Pradip, and Janak, an information technology officer in Uttargaya Rural Municipality in Rasuwa whom Neupane regarded as a cousin.
Sudip survived, only to be haunted by the question of why he lived when the two men beside him did not.

His survival by a whisker means a life tormented by the disaster. Much like hundreds of others who lost their loved ones when a glacial collapse in the Langtang region on August 26 unleashed a devastating flood on the Bhotekoshi river.

After spending two days grieving, Sudip returned to the front line of the relief effort. Displaced people needed food and shelter, and the local unit was short of staff. Some people objected to his presence in relief distribution.

Sudip kept his cool. “We are educated and responsible people. In a disaster, we need to remain calm,” he said. “I survived by luck. For as long as I live, I will continue serving society and the people.”
The morning the flood came
Sudip works as a fourth-level officer in the enterprise development section of Uttargaya Rural Municipality. On August 26, he felt an air of unease.
He did not want to go out that morning. His uncle, who worked at the District Administration Office, warned him before he left. “Son, be careful. There is a flood coming.”
But Sudip felt he had a responsibility to the people around him. As a resident and municipal employee, he believed he needed to help warn villagers of the danger.
Pradip, his younger brother who was a seventh-level public health officer in the rural municipality, joined him. The brothers set out on motorcycles to warn people.
Sudip gave his motorcycle to Pradip, who handed it to health worker Maniram and sat behind him. Sudip travelled on another motorcycle with Janak, locally known as “Janak dai”.
From behind, his younger brother Pradip called out, “Brother, we need to make an announcement!”
Hearing him, Sudip took the microphone and began warning people about the approaching flood as they moved on.

blocks.caption: Relief distribution process underway at Nilakantha Higher Secondary School in Uttargaya Rural Municipality-5 on Thursday.

blocks.text: At Khalte, Sudip warned Pradip not to get any farther. Pradip stopped there while Sudip and Janak continued towards Nayapul.
There they encountered Balaram Neupane, chief of the local health service, rushing back for safety.
“Friends, we won’t survive! We’ll die! Turn back, turn back!” he shouted out.
They turned around and accelerated back towards Khalte. Then came the delay that Sudip believes saved his life.
Buffaloes belonging to displaced members of the Tamang community, who were staying at a temporary camp, were blocking the road.
For roughly two seconds, according to Sudip, they could not move. When the animals cleared out, they continued towards Khalte. The flood struck from behind.
‘It came like a missile’
Sudip says what came down the valley did not feel like an ordinary flood.
“I don’t see it simply as a flood, and it wasn’t an ordinary wave,” he said. “It came like a missile, like artillery. It swept everything away. Nobody even had enough time to make a sound.”
Janak lost control of his motorcycle. He abandoned it and ran towards a field. Neupane ran uphill. The first wave was already behind them.
“Within five minutes of the flood arriving, our office was destroyed,” he said. “In those moments, chances hovered between death and survival. There was no time to pause even for breath.”

Sudip had managed to run for only four or five seconds uphill when the first wave hit. He thought his brother had escaped. Pradip was tall and long-legged. Sudip’s assumption that he could have outrun the water was wrong. He did not survive.
A brother with big dreams
Pradip was 27, had recently built a house and had many plans for the future.
“We came from a poor family. We grew up wearing worn-out clothes and eating whatever food we could afford. We worked hard to build better lives for ourselves,” Sudip recalled.
Their uncle and aunt struggled to support his education, sometimes going without meals to pay for his studies. Pradip eventually earned a master’s in public health.
‘Perhaps I survived for a reason’
Sudip earns about Rs32,000 a month as a municipal employee. The experience has changed his perception of life.
“If we both brothers had died, our family would have been shattered,” he said. “Perhaps that terrifying wave threw me out saying, ‘Now you have to take responsibility for the family.’”
That sense of responsibility helped him overcome grief while people around him were hungry, displaced and needy. “I will help them as much as I can.” /dl

articles.title: Two people rescued alive on 11th day after deadly Nepal floods
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Two people were rescued alive on Saturday, 11 days after devastating floods in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi River left them missing. A Chinese national was rescued from Audit-4 of the Upper…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Two people were rescued alive on Saturday, 11 days after devastating floods in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi River left them missing.
A Chinese national was rescued from Audit-4 of the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa district, the Nepali Army said.

The man had been trapped inside the tunnel since the flooding hit the area. Army spokesman Rajaram Basnet said a team from the Nepali Army, assisted by disaster experts from South Korea, carried out the rescue operation.
He was being taken to an army barracks in Trishuli, Nuwakot, for further care.

blocks.caption: Chandika Shrestha, 64, a resident of Betrawati in Bidur Municipality-10, had gone missing alongside four members of her family on August 26, when the flash floods tore through the Bhotekoshi river basin, decimating entire settlements.  Photo: Courtesy of Nepal Police

blocks.text: Separately, a 64-year-old woman was rescued alive from the upper floor of a four-storey house in Betravati, Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot.

The woman, identified as Chandika Shrestha, had been trapped after the house was buried in the floods. A nine-member rescue team from the army’s No. 19 Battalion, led by Assistant Superintendent of Police Suman Kumar BK, rescued her from the upper floor.
The two rescues came on the 11th day of search and rescue operations following the Bhotekoshi floods, which caused widespread destruction in Rasuwa and surrounding areas. /dl

articles.title: Lacson: Flood control probe should be evidence-based, obstruction-free
articles.summary: Lacson: Flood control probe should be evidence-based , obstruction-free

blocks.text: Published September 6, 2026 11:24am
Senator Panfilo Lacson on Saturday called for an evidence-based investigation into the flood control projects that is free from obstruction.
This came after Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla reported that the Taguig City Hall attempted to prevent his office from conducting its investigation.
In a social media post, Lacson said Senator Alan Peter Cayetano's remarks on the flood control probe exposed of his ignorance on the complex investigation process.

"It only proves Sen Cayetano’s ignorance of how an investigation of flood control anomalies and other sophisticated corruption cases works. It must be deliberate, methodical and thorough; not hasty nor sloppy," Lacson said.
In a separate statement, Cayetano said he could answer Lacson's allegations "point by point", but chooses insted to focus instead on addressing the needs of Filipinos, especially flood victims.
“Although I can answer him (Lacson) point by point… There are more important and urgent things like taking care of people with immediate needs,” he said.
“Araw-araw for the last three months, parang striptease tapos wala namang tunay na ebidensya, panay po akusasyon,” he said.
(Every day for the last three months, it’s been like a striptease, but there’s still no real evidence—just accusations.)
Remulla had said an employee of the Taguig city government tried to prevent Ombudsman investigators from flying a drone to take photographs of the area.

In a dzBB report on Saturday, the Taguig LGU clarified that its Public Order and Safety Office did not hinder the Ombudsman's ongoing investigation following the incident that occurred on Friday morning.
In a statement, the LGU said personnel from its Public Order and Safety Office spotted a black pickup truck parked along the C-6 Road in Taguig.
The people inside the vehicle were wearing civilian clothes and reportedly conducting a drone operation in the area.
The two sides engaged in a heated exchange after the people in the vehicle identified themselves as from the Office of the Ombudsman.
Both parties ended up in a police station where they reached an agreement, and no complaints were filed.
The LGU maintained that its personnel were only performing their duties to help ensure the safety and security of Taguig residents.
Cayetano and Lacson recently engaged in a verbal tussle after the former accused the latter of initiating a “demolition job” over claims on the infrastructure projects in Taguig City.
Lacson, in response, dismissed Cayetano's accusation as "pathetic."
To which Cayetano replied, "Hinahanap lang lahat eh. 'Yung kahit wala, 'yung parang naghanap ka ng multo na wala doon, gumagawa ng storya."
(They’re just trying to find something, even when there’s nothing there. It's like looking for a ghost that doesn’t exist and then creating a story around it.) —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Romualdez must be allowed to answer Bonoan claims, if any, lawyer says
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez should be given the chance to comment on any allegations that may be raised by former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan, his lawyer said…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez should be given the chance to comment on any allegations that may be raised by former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan, his lawyer said on Sunday.

In a statement, Ade Fajardo said Romualdez should be given the chance to refute any new accusations that might be hurled against him, urging “fair play” amid concerns that Bonoan could be pressured to link the former House speaker to the multi-billion peso flood control scandal.
“We are requesting the Ombudsman to inform us if there is any allegation from Secretary Bonoan against former Speaker Romualdez and to give us ample time to comment on it,” Fajardo said.

The lawyer also took note of a report that the Office of the Ombudsman had new witnesses lined up against Romualdez, saying he “would like to know if there is any statement from them against our client.”

“Fair play and due process require that such information and opportunity be accorded to us at this point in the process, the preliminary investigation stage, not if and when the Ombudsman decides to file charges in court,” he added.

Bonoan, who oversaw the buildup of flood control structures, is tied to a corruption scandal involving alleged collusion among state engineers, contractors and politicians to siphon funds meant for mitigation projects that had been poorly built or never existed.
On Thursday, the Sandiganbayan ordered Bonoan’s release after anti-graft prosecutors asked the court to drop him as a co-accused, as they seek to make him a state witness in the corruption scandal.
Romualdez’s lawyers described the withdrawal of plunder charges against Bonoan as alarming.
Fajardo said Bonoan had never linked Romualdez to alleged congressional insertions in last year’s budget and that the latter did not facilitate backroom dealings tied to those allocations.
“There has been no accusation from any of them since this controversy erupted more than a year ago,” Fajardo said.
“Of course, it would surprise us, to say the least, if an allegation surfaces now or in the future.”
Romualdez, has been accused of masterminding a corruption scheme involving budget insertions allegedly funneled to anomalous infrastructure contracts.
He has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing, including claims that he received kickbacks.

The speakership holds significant clout and is typically occupied by an ally of the sitting president. It wields political influence on hundreds of lawmakers representing congressional districts and sectors in the chamber where the yearly national budget originates.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said on Thursday that corruption charges are looming against Romualdez, even though some witnesses had withdrawn statements implicating him. /gsg

articles.title: [Two Pronged] Seasonal Affective Disorder hits, but my therapist’s dead. What now?
articles.summary: 'From the time I wake up to the time I go to sleep the rain never stops... I fear that, if my brain gets used to constantly feeling this down, it will consider this the “new normal” and I have to be…

blocks.text: Rappler’s People section runs an advice column by couple Jeremy Baer and clinical psychologist Dr. Margarita Holmes.

Jeremy has a master’s degree in law from Oxford University. A banker of 37 years who worked in three continents, he has been training with Dr. Holmes for the last 10 years as co-lecturer and, occasionally, as co-therapist, especially with clients whose financial concerns intrude into their daily lives.
Together, they have written two books: Love Triangles: Understanding the Macho-Mistress Mentality and Imported Love: Filipino-Foreign Liaisons.
Dear Dr Holmes and Mr Baer,
I was 12 years old when I took my first antidepressants under the psychiatrist’s guidance. Before that, I was taking whatever my mother was, with her blessing.

By that time, my father could see that my mother was right: I was always sad. This sadness never seemed to leave. Sometimes it was worse than my ordinary sadness like when our kasambahays left without being told why or it rained very hard for several days.
My mother told my father she was the same when a child so he finally agreed to my seeing a psychiatrist too.
My psychiatrist, “Rebo,” was my mother’s psychiatrist and also became my younger brother’s. He saved my life many times.
With my particular depression, it took many years before we realized I was also bipolar. As soon as he prescribed a mood stabilizer, things seemed to make more sense.

We had to try many different mood stabilizers before we found a combination of medicines that finally worked for me day in, day out. Once we discovered what we called the “elixir” life became bearable. Sometimes even more than that.
My biggest success was not changing medication during the pandemic despite the isolation, the mistrust, and the constant loneliness.

Rebo promised I could increase my meds if I needed them increased. But he hoped I wouldn’t need to. He said that my brain might get used to this higher dosage that was really only needed for the pandemic.I managed. I am still on the same meds I have been for the last 16 years. But this weather is worse than the pandemic.

From the time I wake up to the time I go to sleep the rain never stops. I wake up in a cold sweat every morning ever since this ceaseless rain began. I know sunny days appear, but they never last long enough to lift my depressions.
I see no end in sight.
I fear that, if my brain gets used to constantly feeling this down, it will consider this the “new normal” and I have to be on a higher medical regime forever after this.
What is wrong with me?
Should I look for another psychiatrist? Someone who can be my next Rebo? He is no longer (around). He died 2 years ago.
– Ana
Dear Ana,
As Dr Holmes has written an entire book on clinical depression I think it would be foolhardy of me to do other than to defer to her in this instance.
Best wishes,– JAF Baer
Thank you very much for your letter. Let me answer your immediate question first: “Should I look for another psychiatrist?”
Yes.
Second question: “(Should I look for) someone who can be my next “Rebo”?
Absolutely not.

True, Rebo was extremely helpful to you; not just for weeks or months, but for more than 16 years, including the years you were both trying to find the cocktail of meds that could work for you. There is no doubt in my mind that your prognosis would not have been as good were he not your psychiatrist then.

However, sadly, Rebo is no longer around. To look for another Rebo would not make sense, although looking for someone with the qualities you found most helpful would be wise. Very wise.I may be wrong (and if so, please correct me), but I feel Rebo had this rare gift and you were one of the ones blessed enough to have received it.

EXAMPLES: You were right alongside him in your joint quest of getting you better. He was not the one who always knew more than you and thus merely told you what to do. He actually listened to you, and took everything you said, felt, and feared into account. He was not focused on helping you merely with your immediate problem. He was aware that any decision you made now (like upping your meds) might affect the rest of your life.
But much more than that, he showed you the potential implications/ consequences of each action but left you to make the decision.
He treated you like a grown up.

Rebo may have been the best psychiatrist for you then, and may even have been one of the best psychiatrists for you now – if he were around (which sadly “he is no longer”) AND if he would have still been as responsive to this new you, with your new insights, new experiences, new fears, new achievements, new anxieties, etc.
Your job now is to find a psychiatrist whom you can work with smoothly – because you both have the same respect for truth, hard work, facts and wisdom.
Finally, the question which may have been asked merely rhetorically): What is wrong with me?!!?
Nothing that can’t be “fixed.” But this fixing is more of a change in perspective rather than an outside change.

SAD (seasonal affective disorder) is a type of depression linked to changes in seasons, usually starting late fall or winter. Some people suffer from a real depression, SAD, once or more times in their lives.
This can be due to several reasons, such as:

items: a disruption in our circadian rhythm. When things are out of sync, life gets harder… worse if it’s something as major as our biological clock!
a drop in serotonin. Heathcliff lovers may adore dark clouds and cold rain but us ordinary run of the mill lovers can get affected by the lower serotonin levels that we get this time of year;
a Vitamin D Deficiency due to less sunlight. Low vitamin D can negatively affect serotonin levels and worsen mood.

blocks.text: In my opinion, SAD is the West’s answer to our (the East’s) HAD (Habagat affective disorder) or to MAD (Monsoon affective disorder)

Research also shows that SAD is more common in women, young adults, people with a family history of depression, and those living far from the equator where winter days are much shorter. So you have been DOUBLE-WHAMMIED, Ana, by belonging to two risk groups!

Not the best state of affairs, but not the worst either…especially because you know that to be a fact. Thus, being depressed during cold, dark days does not mean something is wrong with you; it merely means you have SAD.
Might I also add that being double-whammied puts you in excellent company. We are now “double-whammied” classmates, Ana!!
All the best,
– MG Holmes
Life got complicated? Write to our Two Pronged duo at twopronged@rappler.com.

articles.title: No verified threats vs VP Sara Duterte, open to receiving reports — PNP
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police said it has not monitored any verified threat against Vice President Sara Duterte or her family, despite her claims that she fears for their safety and has documented…

blocks.text: September 6, 2026 | 10:46am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte shows a document after posting bail at a court building in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) said it has not monitored any verified threat against Vice President Sara Duterte or her family, despite her claims that she fears for their safety and has documented threats and harassment dating back to 2023.
In a statement on Saturday evening, September 5, PNP chief PGen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said Duterte has yet to report to the police any threat to her life or the safety of her family.
“The PNP continues to monitor the situation,” Nartatez said.

"To date, however, the Vice President has not reported to the PNP any threat to her life or to the safety of her family, including the threats she said date back to 2023. Likewise, the PNP has not monitored any verified threat against the Vice President or her family," he added.
Duterte raised the concerns on Saturday when she appeared at the Quezon City Hall of Justice to post bail following the issuance of an arrest warrant against her over three counts of grave threats.
“I have documented threats and harassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them,” Duterte said in a statement issued by the Office of the Vice President.
She also alleged that her family had been subjected to harassment and expressed distrust in both the police and the courts.
“I do not feel safe at all, kahit anong gawin ko,” Duterte said.
Duterte did not provide details about the threats and harassment she said she had documented since 2023. She also did not identify the police officers she referred to in her statements.
The PNP said it provided security assistance during Duterte’s appearance at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98 on Saturday, where she posted P120,000 bail for each of the three counts.
The vice president was able to safely arrive at and leave the court, according to Nartatez.
The PNP said it remains open to receiving documents, reports or statements concerning the alleged threats against Duterte and her family.
"My office, in particular, remains open to receiving such information so that we can properly check, assess, and verify it," Nartatez said.
He also reminded police personnel to comply with the law, observe existing policies and procedures, and perform their duties professionally and lawfully.
Duterte's lawyers said the bail was posted directly with the weekend court, without prejudice to the jurisdictional issues they had raised in the case.
The arrest warrant was issued on Friday, September 4, after the court found probable cause to hold Duterte for trial.

The case stemmed from an online press briefing in November 2024, when Duterte said she had hired someone to kill President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez if she herself were killed.
The Department of Justice charged her with three counts of grave threats under Republic Act 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act.

Duterte's grave threats case comes as her impeachment trial before the Senate is ongoing. The alleged threats against Marcos also form part of one of the Articles of Impeachment against the vice president.
